themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK—a 540% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.2 complaints per week—suggesting concentrated, possibly coordinated tree removal or damage activity in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 8 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.2)
540% spike represents sharpest one-week escalation among environmental complaints
Pattern suggests possible illegal contractor activity or systematic tree removal ahead of development projects (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights rezoning active)
reporting_angles: Map the geographic cluster of complaints—are they concentrated near active construction sites or rezoning areas?
Interview Parks Dept. on enforcement capacity and whether contractors are operating without permits
Cross-reference illegal tree damage complaints with active DOB permits (1231 filed in 90 days, 883 alterations) to identify possible unpermitted work

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 7 LAST WEEK—a 522% increase over the 8-week baseline of 1.1 per week—raising questions about public health, sanitation system failures, or possible pest infestation in the district.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.53)
522% spike indicates acute rather than chronic pattern
Converges with 317% spike in residential disposal complaints (12 last week vs. 2.9 avg), suggesting potential sanitation breakdown
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and NYC Health to determine if there's a known rodent or pest outbreak in the district
Investigate whether trash collection disruptions or missed pickups are driving increased dead animal reports
Interview residents near complaint clusters about visible pest or sanitation issues

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK—a 586% spike over the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week—potentially indicating aging infrastructure problems or contractor-related electrical hazards amid heavy construction activity.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.57)
586% spike in a district with 1231 active DOB permits (100 new buildings, 883 alterations) suggests possible contractor-caused outages or safety hazards
Converges with illegal tree damage spike—both may indicate unsafe or unpermitted construction practices
reporting_angles: Request DOB complaint log to identify electrical violations tied to active permits in the district
Interview Con Edison about service disruptions or voltage issues reported in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights last week
Determine if electrical complaints cluster near major development sites (395 Flatbush, St. Felix, Columbia Heights areas)

themes_detail.label: Police/Investigative Action Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about NYPD Investigations and Discipline (IAD) and Real Time Enforcement surged 2300% and 1729% respectively LAST WEEK, suggesting either intensified police activity in the district or a spike in resident complaints about police conduct.
evidence: IAD complaints: 6 last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 13.28)
Real Time Enforcement complaints: 16 last week vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.36)
Both represent the highest statistical anomalies in dataset; timing suggests either a specific incident or policy change triggered resident complaints
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD, Civilian Complaint Review Board (CCRB), and elected officials to determine if there was a specific enforcement action or incident last week
Review social media and community forums for discussion of police activity in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights that triggered complaints
Interview community advocacy groups about whether residents are mobilizing around a particular incident or pattern of enforcement

themes_detail.label: Construction Debris & Lead Dust Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Construction Lead Dust complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 540% spike over the 8-week baseline of 0.6 per week—raising health concerns about unsafe demolition or renovation practices amid 1231 active DOB permits in the district.
evidence: 4 construction lead dust complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85)
540% spike amid 883 active alteration permits suggests possible lead-paint violations in older Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights housing stock
Converges with illegal tree damage and electrical spikes—pattern suggests broad contractor safety/compliance concerns
reporting_angles: Cross-reference lead dust complaints with DOB permit database to identify which contractors/projects are cited
Interview NYC Health Department about enforcement of lead abatement rules during renovations in the district
Report on whether aging pre-1978 buildings in the area are receiving adequate lead inspections before renovation work begins
